title: The City That Couldn't Stop Dancing #shorts

lines.text: Can a whole city dance until it drops? In fifteen eighteen, Strasbourg did.
In July, a woman named Frau Troffea began dancing in the street, and she danced for days.
Within weeks, as many as four hundred people had joined her.
Doctors blamed hot blood, so officials hired a band and built a stage to dance it out.
It backfired. Many collapsed from exhaustion, and some reportedly died.
Historians still argue why, from moldy rye to pure mass stress.
So, can a city dance until it drops? In Strasbourg it did, and nobody could stop the music.

facts.start: July 1518, Frau Troffea danced in the street for nearly a week (History.com)
facts.spread: about three dozen joined, reportedly up to ~400 by August (History.com)
facts.response: physicians blamed 'hot blood' and advised dancing it out; officials built a stage, hired musicians and professional dancers (History.com)
facts.toll: many collapsed from exhaustion; some reportedly died of strokes/heart attacks (death toll is disputed)
facts.causes: ergot-mold poisoning vs mass psychogenic illness / St. Vitus belief (John Waller)
